In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the anti-VH antibody reacts with an epitope on a V mu fragment that is not expressed on the intact Ig molecule and which appears to be expressed in the plasma cell but not the B cell stage of B cell maturation.
the anti-VH monoclonal antibodies react with "hidden" determinants that are expressed on B cells and plasma cells, but not on T cells, and that are not exposed on intact, undenatured Ig molecules.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the VH determinants recognized by monoclonal anti-idiotypic antibodies are expressed in the B lineage of cells at all stages of development, but are not expressed on T cells, even in the activated state.

monoclonal antibodies have been produced that react with VH determinants that are hidden on intact Ig molecules and that are expressed at different stages of differentiation of normal B cells and plasma cells.
the anti-VH monoclonal antibodies react with a new class of VH determinants that are expressed by subpopulations of plasma cells and B cells but not by T cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the monoclonal antibodies we have produced can be used for a variety of purposes, including the identification of VH+ B lymphocyte subpopulations, for the analysis of VH genes and gene products, for the study of the regulation of VH gene expression, for the identification of VH genes rearranged in human lymphomas, and for the study of VH genes rearrangement during B cell ontogeny.
there are hidden VH determinants in human immunoglobuline molecules that are not exposed on intact immunoglobulin and that can be used for immunological analysis of human lymphocytes.
the anti-VH monoclonal antibodies can be used to identify and enumerate B lymphocytes at different stages of maturation and differentiation in the normal human lymphoid system.
